answers.explanation: Loading and running a program is the program-execution service.
Writing files and managing their permissions are both file-system manipulation.
Exchanging information between computers over a network is communications.
Deciding who gets an I/O device is resource allocation.
Noticing an I/O device error and taking the right action is error detection.
Tracking who used how much is accounting; billing is one use of it.
A running program needing a device is the I/O-operations service.
Authenticating users keeps outsiders out: security.
The OS detects the error and protection keeps the bad access from harming anyone else.
